title: Cochinita Pibil
equipment: dutch oven or heavy pot with a lid

qty.note: about 1/3 cup from a block or tub

qty.unit: limes (1 juiced for the onions, 1 in wedges)

steps.text: Blend the achiote, orange juice, lime juice, garlic, cumin, oregano, and salt into a smooth, brick-red marinade. It will stain whatever it touches.
Rub the pork all over with the marinade. Rest 30 minutes on the counter (or cover and refrigerate overnight — better).
Heat the oven to 325°F. Heat the oil in the dutch oven and brown the pork chunks on two sides, about 6 minutes total, then lift them out.

Return the pork and any escaped marinade to the pot, clamp on the lid, and braise 3 hours. Pork shoulder is safe at 145°F (63°C), but a low braise takes it far past — check the thickest chunk on a thermometer.

safety.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperature table

steps.text: Rest the pot, covered, off the heat for 15 minutes. Then shred the pork with two forks right in its juices.
While it rests, toss the sliced red onion with the juice of 1 lime and a pinch of salt; squeeze and knead it once. In 20 minutes it slumps into bright pink pickled onions.
Toast the tortillas in a dry skillet until pliable and freckled. Build tacos: pork, pickled onion, a squeeze of lime.
Leftovers keep 4 days chilled or 3 months frozen. Reheat gently in a covered skillet with a splash of water until the pork reaches 165°F (74°C) on a thermometer.

cuisine_note: Cochinita pibil is Yucatan's celebration pork: achiote and sour-orange marinade, wrapped and pit-roasted, then pulled apart in its own juices. A dutch oven at 325°F is the honest home-oven version.
